newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 27.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 27.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Monday:
* Indonesia's import growth rate declined to 4.8 percent in 1996 compared with 30.5 percent in the previous year, the official Antara news agency reported on Saturday.

* Wall Street stocks, struggling for their footing after a sharp pullback, will turn this week to the fourth quarter Employee Cost Index report due on Tuesday, a barometer of how much companies pay for employees, and fourth-quarter earnings reports.
Analysts said a higher-than-expected ECI number could damage the inflation-sensitive bond market and rekindle fears of a Federal Reserve hike in interest rates.
* As fears of rising interest rates mounted, the Dow Jones industrial average fell 59.27 points to end the week at 6,696.48, down nearly 200 points from its record close of 6,883.90 on Tuesday.
* Indonesian government is proposing a new regulation which would require companies to submit audited financial reports if they have loans from banks or non-bank financial institutions.
* The Jakarta composite index fell 6.07 points, or 0.89 percent, to close at 678.91 points on Friday, pulled down by profit-taking in heavyweights.
* On Monday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,374.50/74.75 in early trading against the opening of 2,374.00/74.50.
* Hotel Prapatan on reports it expected strong 1996 results following launch of new restaurants in 1996.
* Mulialand on reports its majority stakeholder has proposed to issue exchangable bonds to finance Mulialand's property project in West Jakarta.
* Bimantara on news it was expected to sell its stake in tyre firm PT Intirub.
* Lippo Securities on reports its 1996 net profit was expected to be better-than-expected.
* Bank BNI on market talk of a possible better-than-expected 1996 net profit.
* Tapioca starch maker Budi Acid on reports it was in negotiations to set up two joint ventures with local and Japanese firms.
